pride_data.title: Elucidating PTEN Conformational Dynamics and Phosphatase Regulation via Integrative Modeling and Mutation Prediction
pride_data.projectDescription: PTEN (Phosphatase and TENsin homolog deleted on chromosome ten) is a major tumor suppressor gene that is frequently mutated or lost under cancerous conditions. PTEN is a dual-specificity phosphatase that negatively regulates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway at the plasma membrane (PM). Its functional regulation and cellular localization are known to be conformationally driven. Access to the PM is phospho-regulated by open and closed PTEN forms. However, clarifying the underlying structural mechanisms is still an open avenue of research. Here, we apply an integrative structural modeling approach, combining coarse-grained and all-atom molecular dynamics with experimental crosslinking mass spectrometry. Conformational exchange between an “eased” form and a “strained” form brings the protein’s phosphatase and C2 domains closer together, blocking the catalytic site, and affecting the loops involved in PM binding. Our full-length PTEN models, AlphaMissense, and RaSP were used to better predict the consequences of PTEN mutations.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: TThese samples were also analyzed using a data dependent method as well as a MS2-MS3 cross-linking methods.   This method involved a CID based MS2 fragmentation at a lower energy (25%) CID with high resolution detection in the Orbitrap (30000).  Peptides that have the DSSO or DHSO diagnostic mass difference of 31.9721 Da were selected for an MS3 experiment performed in the ion trap.  For the data-dependent and XL-MS analysis, collected data were queried against the sequence of PTEN (P60484) using Sequest bundled into Proteome Discoverer 2.5 (ThermoScientific). Parameters included full tryptic peptides, 2 missed cleavages, protein acetylation at the N-terminus, methionine oxidation, DSSO modification of lysine residues (DSSO samples), and DMTMM (DHSO samples) as variable modifications, carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification, protein mass tolerance of 10 ppm, and fragment ion mass tolerance of 0.6 Da. Protein and peptide validation was performed using a decoy database strategy with Percolator with a peptide and protein level false discovery rate kept at <1% (see ref below) to identify high-confidence proteins. The criteria used for protein identification included at least two identified peptides, one unique peptide, and a Sequest score > 4.0. XL-MS data were analyzed using the XLinkX 2.2 (see ref below) node bundled with Proteome Discoverer 2.5. Parameters were as above with the addition of DSSO as the cross-linker and 3 missed cleavages. This data was searched against the human SwissProtKB database and specifically against the sequence of PTEN (P60484). Validation of cross-linked peptides was done using Percolator (Matrix Science) with an FDR set at 1%. A consensus workflow was also applied for the statistical arrangement; de-isotope and TopX filters were used to determine m/z error with selectivity set to ~10% FDR.  Each XL-MS spectra that were designated as high confidence were inspected for the following criteria; MS3 spectra from three of the four possible fragments need to contain sequence specific y and b ions consistent with the amino acid makeup of the peptide.  Sites of cross-linking were determined in XlinkX searches and manually validated.
